plan: Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Add to QQQI, bringing it to 20%, for income and broad index exposure.
Sell QQQ, SMH, SOXL, and SPAL entirely due to sell flags, being below stops, or as part of cutting all leveraged ETFs.

conservative.read: This conservative approach targets around 1.5% per month, focusing on capital preservation. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest growth potential. The primary risk is underperforming in strong bull markets.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Sell QQQ and SMH due to sell flags and being below stops.
Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 1% to reduce overall leveraged ETF exposure.
Buy SLB at 4% and XLV at 5% as strong new long setups from the scanner.
This plan balances risk and growth, maintaining a small leveraged ETF presence.
balanced.read: This balanced approach aims for around 2.5% per month, prioritizing risk-first growth. It blends broad index with quality tech and some small leverage. Expect moderate volatility and drawdowns, with potential for solid growth.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Sell QQQ due to its sell flag.
Trim SMH to 5% as it is below its stop, but maintain some exposure.
Add to SOXL to 6% and SPAL to 6%, increasing leveraged ETF exposure within limits.

aggressive.read: This aggressive approach targets around 4% per month, stretching for growth. It uses and adds leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups. Be aware of significantly higher volatility, potential for larger drawdowns, and the daily decay/rebalancing of leveraged ETFs. Strict stop discipline is crucial.

plan: Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and meet the mandate.
Add to QQQI, bringing it to 30%, to significantly increase income focus.
Sell QQQ, CRWD, SMH, SOXL, and SPAL entirely due to sell flags, being below stops, or as part of cutting leverage and high-beta names.

income.read: This income approach aims for around 1% per month, focusing on parking cash for yield. It rotates into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index, cutting leverage and high-beta names. Distributions are variable and NAV can still fall; this is not a savings account, but prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income.
